_comment: Secrets commonly pasted into prompts — text API only (docs/DECISIONS.md D-015), active whatever the theme.
Every format is checked against the provider's official documentation or the standard; the source is in each pattern name.
Presidio compiles these with the `regex` module and IGNORECASE|DOTALL|MULTILINE: case-sensitive prefixes use (?-i:...),
quantifiers are possessive to rule out catastrophic backtracking (tests/test_text_api_recognizers.py, ReDoS probe).
Score 0.9: above every theme threshold (0.4) — a secret is never filtered by score.

patterns.name: PEM private key block, complete (RFC 7468 s.2 and s.10-11 'PRIVATE KEY' / 'ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY'; OpenSSH sshkey.c MARK_BEGIN 'OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY'; RFC 9580 s.6.2.1 'PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK'; legacy RSA/EC/DSA labels); case-insensitive markers: main.py capitalizes all-caps words before analysis ('RSA PRIVATE KEY' reaches Presidio as 'Rsa Private Key')

PEM private key header and base64 body without END line (truncated paste), same sources; case-insensitive markers: main.py capitalizes all-caps words before analysis ('RSA PRIVATE KEY' reaches Presidio as 'Rsa Private Key')
JWT compact serialization, base64url JSON header and payload starting with eyJ, signature possibly empty (RFC 7519 s.3.1 and s.6.1)
URI with user:password@ userinfo, any scheme: postgresql://, mysql://, mongodb+srv://, redis://, amqp://, https://... (RFC 3986 s.3.2.1)
Azure shared access signature 'sig=' parameter (Microsoft Learn, Configure a connection string - Azure Storage, SAS examples)

value assigned to a password/token/secret/api_key key (key = value, key: value, "key": "value", 'mot de passe est ...'), including Azure 'AccountKey=' and 'SharedAccessSignature=' (Microsoft Learn, Configure a connection string - Azure Storage) and AWS 'aws_secret_access_key'; same line only, and not a code expression (value followed by '(' or '[': os.getenv(...), config.get(...), headers[...])
HTTP Authorization header credentials: Bearer token (RFC 6750 s.2.1 b64token) or Basic (RFC 7617 s.2)

AWS access key ID: prefixes AKIA (access key), ASIA (temporary STS), ABIA (STS bearer token), ACCA (context-specific credential) (AWS IAM User Guide, Understanding unique ID prefixes); total length 16-128, pattern [\w]* (AWS STS API Reference, Credentials); only the leading 'A' is case-sensitive: an all-letters key is capitalized by main.py's normalization ('Akia...')
Google Cloud API key, prefix AIza (Google Cloud, Manage API keys: example AIzaSyDaGmWKa4JsXZ-HjGw7ISLn_3namBGewQe)
GitHub tokens ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_, github_pat_ (GitHub Docs, About authentication to GitHub, GitHub's token formats)
GitLab tokens glpat-, gloas-, gldt-, glrt-, glrtr-, glcbt-, glptt-, glft-, glimt-, glagent-, glwt-, glsoat-, glffct- (GitLab Docs, GitLab token overview, token prefixes)
Slack tokens xoxb-, xoxp-, xwfp-, xapp-, xoxe.xapp- (Slack Developer Docs, Tokens)
Telegram bot token: numeric id, colon, string (Telegram Bot API, Authorizing your bot: example 123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11)

Stripe secret and restricted keys sk_live_, sk_test_, rk_live_, rk_test_, organization keys sk_org_ (Stripe Docs, API keys; publishable pk_ keys are public by design and NOT matched), webhook signing secret whsec_ (Stripe Docs, Webhooks)
